description: skill-guard: deny noisy skills inline in the main context and tell the model to run them in a separate agent (use-agents picks the carrier). worktree-guard: enforce exit-safety order on git worktree remove. skill-atlas-guard: block commits with stale skill-fleet evidence or any Skill & Doc Style finding. skill-path-fallback: deny a Bash command with an unexpanded ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and tell the model how to resolve the real script path. learn-capture (Stop) + session-replay (SessionStart): the [LEARN] sedimentation loop — capture markers into .claude/LEARNED.md, replay last 5 at session start, plus the rules digest ccobs rollup built for this project (plain stdout, no model call; Codex ignores hookSpecificOutput on SessionStart). recall-precedent (UserPromptSubmit): once per session, on the first prompt long enough to describe a task, inject up to 3 past sessions of this project that match it, each with its transcript path — picked by a cheap model through pi headless (openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna:low, ~6s on a 60-row catalog), capped at 12s, silent on any failure. Output shape differs by event on purpose: SessionStart injects via plain stdout because Codex drops hookSpecificOutput there, UserPromptSubmit injects via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext because Claude Code drops plain stdout there — and Codex reads hookSpecificOutput on this event, verified live, so no per-client branch is needed. Every hook sits in its own group because Codex runs only the first hook of a group. plan-anchor (SessionStart source=compact): replay the live plan's locked constraints (reference source / done-means / out-of-scope) that compaction drops. security-warning-relay (PostToolUse Agent): a subagent's SECURITY WARNING gets surfaced to the user, not read past. compact-audit (PostCompact): record which plan anchors each compaction summary dropped, into ~/.claude/observability/compaction.jsonl — no model call, substring checks only. obs-enqueue (Stop): append this session to ccobs' queue.jsonl for near-real-time ingest — one line, milliseconds, no model call.
